item.title: Senate fails to advance Clarity Act, a sweeping crypto bill
item.description: The Senate on Tuesday failed to advance a sweeping cryptocurrency bill called the Clarity Act, amid opposition from Democrats and some Republicans. Nikhilesh De, managing editor for global policy and regulations at CoinDesk, joins CBS News to discuss.

item.title: Russia sanctions bill co-authored by late Sen. Lindsay Graham advances
item.description: A bipartisan Russia sanctions bill, championed by the late Sen. Graham and designed to pressure the country into ending its war with Ukraine, has been approved by the House Rules Committee. CBS News contributor Masih Alinejad joins to discuss her support for the bill.

item.title: Major Garrett says Steely Dan isn't "Yacht Rock"
item.description: Major Garrett has a hostile issue with Merrian-Webster's new definition of "Yacht Rock," which noted Steely Dan as an example of the genre. "Including Steely Dan is a travesty of justice and an affont to its musical, lyrical and stylistic originality," Major says.

item.title: Delaware holds U.S. Senate primary and more races to watch today
item.description: Delaware Sen. Chris Coons is seeking a third full term.

item.title: Father and daughter pilots happen to cross paths over air traffic control
item.description: Just before taking off for Munich, Germany, United Airlines pilot Kent Katnik, checked in with the tower and heard his daughter, Kenny Katnick, herself a pilot, about to take off for Syracuse. Tony Dokoupil has the story.

item.title: Former Indiana Gov. Mitch Daniels on new book about working in Reagan, Bush 43 White Houses
item.description: Former Indiana Gov. Mitch Daniels has written a new memoir about his life in both the Reagan and George W. Bush White Houses, as well as his time as president of Purdue University. Daniels joined "The Takeout" to discuss, "Impatience is a Virtue."

item.title: Nick Reiner will not face death penalty if convicted of his parents' murders
item.description: Los Angeles County District Attorney Nathan Hochman told reporters his office considered the views of Nick's siblings, Jake and Romy, when making the decision.

item.title: New photos show widespread damage at U.S. positions caused by Iranian attacks
item.description: The images were sent to CBS News by active service members under condition of anonymity.

item.title: Arch Manning apologizes for laughing at violent AI video towards reporter Holly Rowe
item.description: Arch Manning, one of the most famous names in college football, coming off one of the biggest wins of his life on Saturday, made one of his bigger blunters. He laughed and joked about an AI video of Steve Sarkisian hitting reporter Holly Rowe. He has since apologized.

item.title: New images show widespread damage at U.S. bases in Middle East after Iran attacks
item.description: New images obtained exclusively by CBS News reveal devastating damage across U.S. bases in the Middle East after missile and drone strikes from Iran. CBS News' Jonah Kaplan has more.

item.title: Newsom tells CNN he won't run for president if Kamala Harris does in 2028
item.description: California Gov. Gavin Newsom told CNN that he will not run for president in 2028 if Kamala Harris launches her own campaign. Political strategists Kendra Barkoff Lamy and Marc Short join "The Takeout" to discuss.

item.title: In Washington, unlikely bedfellows like Bernie Sanders and Steve Bannon talk about making AI "humans first"
item.description: As AI CEOs call for a slowdown, President Trump wants acceleration. But the issue is gaining bipartisan momentum.

item.title: Trump admin. will comply with mail ballot ruling by Supreme Court, Blanche says
item.description: The Supreme Court on Monday blocked the Postal Service from enforcing new mail voting rules ahead of the midterm elections.

item.title: Patel pushed on lower hiring standards at FBI, Olympic celebration
item.description: FBI Director Kash Patel​ was grilled for nearly five hours by both Democrats and Republicans about a string of recent negative headlines about the FBI.

item.title: Fireworks triggered deadly wildfire in Washington state, investigators believe
item.description: In Washington state, investigators said they believe illegal fireworks, shot from the back of a pickup truck, sparked a nearly 10,000-acre deadly wildfire earlier this summer. Jason Allen reports.

item.title: Democrats have clear edge over Republicans in midterms with Trump approval at 38%, new poll shows
item.description: A new New York Times/Siena poll shows likely voters favor Democratic candidates in their districts by around 8 percentage points over Republicans. The same poll also found President Trump's approval rating sitting at 38%. Kyle Kondik, managing editor for Sabato's Crystal Ball, joins "The Takeout" to discuss.

item.title: Zelenskyy says "of course" Putin is lying to Trump officials
item.description: President Volodymyr Zelenskyy sat down for an exclusive interview with CBS News' Aiden Stretch about what he said were recent Russian plots to assassinate him. Zelenskyy also discussed President Trump's new demand that Ukraine stop attacking Russian energy targets to help gas prices in the U.S.

item.title: Ed Sheeran's supporting acts pull out of tour after Macklemore was dropped
item.description: Aaron Rowe, Beoga, Lukas Graham and Finneas all released statements Tuesday on Instagram saying they were withdrawing from Ed Sheeran's tour.

item.title: Ed Sheeran breaks silence after Macklemore dropped from tour
item.description: The rapper Macklemore was bumped from Ed Sheeran's U.S. concert tour for pro-Palestinian comments that some say crossed a line into prejudice. Now, four additional supporting acts have quit in solidarity and the headliner has addressed the controversy. Carter Evans reports.

item.title: Key moments from FBI Director Kash Patel's Senate hearing
item.description: FBI Director Kash Patel testified before the Senate Judiciary Committee on Tuesday, defending his lowering of hiring standards and saying the bureau had no plans to seize election-related materials. CBS News' Jake Rosen has more.

item.title: Smart glasses capture stolen Tesla barreling down San Diego boardwalk, man pinning down suspect
item.description: A man racing a stolen Tesla down a crowded boardwalk hit a woman, setting off a wild chase involving lots of witnesses, including one recording it all on a pair of smart glasses. Jonah Kaplan reports.

item.title: FBI says it foiled an ISIS-inspired plot in Pennsylvania
item.description: The FBI said it thwarted a "mass casualty attack," inspired by ISIS, allegedly by a 21-year-old man in Pennsylvania. Agents allegedly tracked the young man to a hotel where they arrested him. It's the second ISIS-related plot to surface since August. Nicole Sganga reports.

item.title: H.R. McMaster on CBO report that Iran war has cost $38 billion: "It's worth it"
item.description: Former Trump national security adviser H.R. McMaster joins "The Takeout" to discuss Tuesday's report from the Congressional Budget Office showing that the Iran war has cost an estimated $38 billion from Feb. 28 to Aug. 1.

item.title: Blanche says White House will comply with ruling that blocks new USPS rules for mail ballots
item.description: Attorney General Todd Blanche conducted the White House press briefing on Tuesday, commenting on the Supreme Court's ruling that blocks President Trump's new postal service rules for mail ballots. CBS News' Ed O'Keefe has more.

item.title: Family blames Texas' "merciless" abortion ban for woman's death, sues Paxton, others
item.description: The family of 37-year-old Tierra Walker filed a lawsuit against Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton and others, saying she was denied an abortion that could have saved her life.

item.title: FBI investigation thwarts "mass casualty attack" from man accused of ISIS allegiance
item.description: Federal officials said Jonathan Kramer had armed himself to carry out a mass casualty attack against the American people.

item.title: Sen. Bernie Sanders, Steve Bannon appear at same AI safety rally
item.description: The AI debate made for strange bedfellows Tuesday as progressive Sen. Bernie Sanders and MAGA provocateur Steve Bannon appeared at the same event calling for human-centered AI decisions. CBS News' Caitlin Huey-Burns has more.

item.title: CBS News speaks with Taliban spokesperson 25 years after 9/11
item.description: CBS News' Imtiaz Tyab sits down with Taliban spokesperson Abdul Qahar Balkhi, five years after the group's return to power in Afghanistan. They discuss the Taliban's claims of peace and stability, the country's ongoing humanitarian crisis and restrictions on women and girls, as well as U.S. military hardware, frozen assets, future U.S.-Afghanistan relations and lessons from two decades of war.

item.title: White House backs Hegseth as new details come out about Iran war's cost
item.description: The Iran war has cost the U.S. military at least $33.4 billion — most of it on munitions — and not including hundreds of millions more spent by other agencies, the Pentagon says.

item.title: Sanders says potential danger of AI is "probably greater" than nuclear weapons
item.description: Sen. Bernie Sanders is one of the most vocal opponents in Congress on rapid AI development, but bipartisan concerns are growing.
